name: Reward-pool minority game: simulate where rival farmers will quote tomorrow and sit where they will not
one_line: Treat liquidity-reward allocation as a repeated minority game. A population model of rival makers forecasts next-day dilution per pool, and the LP bot allocates to the best predicted reward per unit of jump risk.
scope: Data: the public /rewards/markets/multi endpoint, which worked without auth today and exposes market_competitiveness, rate_per_day, max spread and volume_24hr. Add the bot's own /rewards/user/percentages and the public distributor payout logs. Model: a heterogeneous farmer population of rate-chasers, competitiveness-chasers, category specialists and sponsored-pool sprinters. Crowd-anticrowd dynamics predict overshoot, so pools that looked empty yesterday are crowded today. Combine this with a jump-risk score built from scheduled catalysts and category gap and dispute rates, so that 'uncontested' does not mean 'gap-risk dump'. Evidence from the E2 pack, not re-fetched: 16,719 pools configured at $585k a day against $108-156k a day actually paid. Rate divided by competitiveness spans seven orders of magnitude. 23.5% of configured rate sits in competitiveness-0 markets. The top 10 wallets take 24%, and the median payout is about $5. In the Telonex case, makers doubled within a day of a sponsorship. Fetched today: five NFL moneylines with identical $15,771-a-day pools show competitiveness from 1.28 to 8.78. Validation: 30 days of hourly snapshots. First test whether the population model beats persistence at predicting next-day competitiveness. Then A/B the allocator against rate-ranked allocation, net of markout.
why_it_matters: The owner already runs LP. The E2 pack says ranking pools by rate_per_day is wrong by about 4x in aggregate. Nobody models the farmers as a population, and the co-evolution gym in the list trains agents and does not allocate. No event forecasting is needed. Feedback is daily, so validation is fast. This is 'trade created by simulating the competitors', a lens no entry uses.
flags: Use one identity only. No self-matching, because rebates and rewards are forfeitable retroactively (E9 pack). market_competitiveness is undocumented and can change. Reward parameters move without notice. Uncontested pools are disproportionately gap-risk markets (E2 pack). This may belong in the incentives band, so route it if that band has no equivalent.

key_evidence.note: Polymarket CLOB API, fetched 2026-09-20 without auth. Five NFL moneylines at $15,771.43 a day and max spread 2.5c show competitiveness 1.28, 1.65, 2.64, 3.42 and 8.78.
[pre-2025] Hart, Jefferies, Johnson, Hui 2000: the crowd-anticrowd model of the Minority Game, the adjacent-field template for predicting crowding (arXiv listing only).
[pre-2025] Ruch, Wakeling, Zhang 2002: the interactive minority game, with crowded, efficient and critical phases (arXiv listing only).
